phases.decides: First reading and public hearing September 8 and second reading and public hearing September 22 (both 5:30 p.m.) adopt the millage and the FY 2027 budget; a budget workshop was held September 14.

levers.how: Speak during the Comments and Questions portion of the meeting on any city business, or on an agenda item when it is heard. The council rules encourage signing in with the City Clerk before the meeting starts.
levers.rules: Comments and Questions: one appearance per person, three minutes. Agenda items: up to three speakers in favor and three against, three minutes each. No signs or placards in the chamber. Lobbyists must register with the City Clerk.
levers.deadline: Sign in with the Clerk before the meeting begins

levers.how: Email comments to CityClerk@hialeahfl.gov; they are read into the record for up to three minutes. Visual material to be shown during your comments must go to the Clerk's office ahead of time.
levers.rules: For the October 27, 2026 meeting the email deadline was 3:00 p.m. Thursday October 22 (five days before) and the visual-material deadline 5:00 p.m. October 6; each meeting notice sets its own dates.
levers.deadline: About five days before the meeting, per the meeting notice

levers.how: Call City Hall or email the City Clerk, who forwards to the Mayor and Council.
Submit a public records request through the City Clerk, the custodian of public records.
Florida's uniform municipal recall statute, F.S. 100.361, applies to Hialeah council members and the Mayor; the charter text could not be checked for a city-specific provision.
levers.rules: Under F.S. 100.361, in a city with 25,000 or more registered electors the petition needs 1,000 electors or 5 percent, whichever is greater, gathered within 30 days and filed with the clerk within 30 days of the first signature.

levers.how: File qualification papers, the qualifying fee and the assessment with the City Clerk during the qualifying period (City Code Sec. 34-2; Charter Art. V Sec. 5.05). Candidates must be resident electors (Sec. 5.01); elections are nonpartisan (Sec. 5.02).
levers.rules: Qualifying has run from noon on the first Monday of July to 5:00 p.m. three weeks later (2025: July 7 to July 28; 2026 special: July 6 to July 27). Term limits: Mayor two consecutive terms, Council three consecutive terms (Sec. 2.02(d)).
levers.deadline: 5:00 p.m. on the last day of the July qualifying period

levers.how: Regular city elections are held in November of odd years (primary the first Tuesday after the first Monday, run-off general in December); the 2026 Group II special election is on the November 3, 2026 ballot. Vote through Miami-Dade Elections.
levers.deadline: November 3, 2026 special primary; December 8, 2026 run-off if needed

levers.how: Board appointments are made at council meetings (a standing Board Appointments agenda item); ask the City Clerk about openings.

elections.terms: Mayor four years, limit two consecutive terms. Seven council members elected at large by group number for four-year terms, limit three consecutive terms. Groups elected in November 2025: Mayor and Groups V, VI, VII (full terms) plus III and IV (special). Group II special election November 3, 2026 fills a term ending November 5, 2027; the next regular election is November 2027 (Groups I, II, III, IV expected).
